subject: Sharing: security assessment - redaction checklist & NDA carve-outs
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-cloud.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: full security assessment & pen report access

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the call last week. Our security team is preparing the vendor assessment for the upcoming SOC 2 refresh and SIG. Can you provide the most recent security assessment and the penetration test report (full PDF) for Redwood Inference?

We generally handle these under a standard non-disclosure; if you prefer, we can sign your mutual NDA. If possible, please include:
- Exec summary (no redaction)
- Full report under NDA
- A short remediation status matrix (open/closed/in-progress with ETA)

If there are any export or redaction constraints, please call those out. We can expedite review on our side.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reyes
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Cloud Services

Attachment: request_template.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: full security assessment & pen report access

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks. We can definitely share the requested materials but have two constraints to flag up front:
1) The full penetration test contains customer-identifying data and PoC artifacts that must be redacted before external distribution.
2) We require an executed NDA with the redaction carve-outs we typically use (limited distribution, no screenshots of customer environments, and no publishing).

Proposed approach:
- I'll circulate a redacted executive summary now (PDF) that omits customer-specific IP and PoC details — intended for immediate review.
- For the full report, we can deliver a version under NDA with our proposed redaction matrix applied (see attachment) and a remediation status matrix indicating current owner and ETA.
- If Acme legal prefers, we can review their mutual NDA; our legal team has a couple of non-negotiables (see bullets below).

Non-negotiables (summary):
- Distribution limited to Acme security and legal teams for assessment purposes only
- No publication or sharing with third-party media/vendors without prior written consent
- Redaction responsibility: Redwood will apply redactions; Acme may request additional redactions but must sign off on final copy

Looping in Karthik (security) for the remediation matrix and Marissa (contracts) for NDA coordination.

Best,
Mina
Director, Trust & Security — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redaction_guidance_matrix.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-cloud.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: full security assessment & pen report access

Thanks Mina — that approach sounds reasonable. Quick clarifications from our side before we sign:
- Can you confirm what you consider "customer-identifying data"? For example, do IP ranges and S3 bucket names fall into that category?
- We typically prefer the vendor to apply redactions and provide a short markup of redaction locations.
- For timelines: if we sign an NDA today, when can we expect the full redacted report?

Also attaching Acme's standard Mutual NDA for your legal team to review. It's a short form and usually accepted with minimal edits.

Regards,
Tom

Attachment: Acme_MUTUAL_NDA_v3.docx (DOCX)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-cloud.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: full security assessment & pen report access

Tom —

Quick technical clarifications to help scope redactions:
- "Customer-identifying" for us includes: customer names, tenant IDs, specific S3 bucket names, private IP ranges that are routeable to a single customer, and full PoC exploit code that reveals customer configuration.
- We consider public IP ranges that are shared across multiple tenants (e.g., our front-end LB) as non-identifying unless linked to a customer-specific hostname.
- PoC artifacts that demonstrate a vulnerability but don't include config dumps can be summarized rather than included verbatim.

ETA: once NDA is executed and we have written confirmation of the permitted reviewers, we can produce a redacted full report within 5 business days. The remediation matrix (snapshot) is attached; items marked "in-progress" include owner and expected closure quarter.

Karthik
Head of Applied Security — Redwood Inference

Attachments: remediation_matrix_snapshot.csv (CSV)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-cloud.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: full security assessment & pen report access

Tom —

Thanks for sending your NDA. Our counsel reviewed Acme_MUTUAL_NDA_v3 and proposed two narrow edits:
1) Add an explicit distribution list clause (we ask that Acme confirm the reviewer list in writing when returning the signed NDA).
2) Remove the unilateral indemnity clause on Section 6; we propose substitution language that limits liability in the typical vendor assessment context.

I'm attaching a redacted executive summary (redacted_exec_summary_v1.pdf) for your immediate review as discussed. If those two legal edits are acceptable, we can sign a mutual NDA quickly or accept the attached signed Redwood Addendum (DocuSign link below) that includes the edits.

Next steps we propose:
- Acme to confirm reviewer list in reply to this thread.
- Legal teams to confirm NDA edits (I can provide a tracked-change version).
- Once NDA signed, Redwood will deliver the redacted full report within 5 business days.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
